info.name: Civicon — Auth & Issues
info.description:
Auth, identity and civic issue reporting for the Civicon backend.

Start the API with `npm run start:dev` and seed it with `npm run seed` — every seeded account uses the password in {{demo_password}}.

Folders run top to bottom: later requests reuse tokens and ids that earlier ones set.

variable.description: Shared by every account created by `npm run seed`.
Set automatically by any sign-in request.
Used to prove the 401 messages are identical.
Set by 'Sign in as a second citizen'.

item.description: The only routes reachable without a token. Everything else returns 401 — the guards are registered globally, so a route is protected unless it opts out with @Public().

item.name: Auth
item.description:
Sign-up and sign-in. Both register and login return { token, user }; the token's claims carry the user's roles, so guards need no database round-trip.

Login and register write `token` and `user_id` into the collection variables, so every later request is authenticated automatically.

request.description:
Registration always creates a CITIZEN. There is no `roles` field to send — volunteering is an action a citizen takes, not a role they hold, and AGENCY / SPONSOR / ADMIN come from the seed or an admin grant.

The email carries a random suffix so the collection can be re-run: the seed already owns the fixed addresses, and a duplicate returns 409.

item.name: Users (admin only)
item.description:
User administration, restricted to ADMIN. There is no POST /users — registration is the only account-creation path, since a second one would produce users with no password.

This folder is self-contained: it signs in as the seeded admin, creates a disposable user to operate on, and deletes it at the end. Safe to run end-to-end.

request.description: Seeded by `npm run seed`.
Registered with a random email so the folder can be re-run. Its id lands in `target_user_id`.
Requires ADMIN. The password hash is absent from every response: the schema marks it `select: false` and the toJSON transform deletes it.
A malformed id returns 400 (not 500) via ParseObjectIdPipe; a well-formed but unknown id returns 404.
UpdateUserDto carries no `roles` field, so this route cannot be used to escalate privileges — see the Guardrails folder.

The admin-only path by which AGENCY, SPONSOR and ADMIN accounts come into existence.

Replace semantics: the array supplied becomes the user's roles, so this revokes as well as grants. AGENCY implies nothing, so CITIZEN is dropped here.
Returns 204 No Content.

item.name: Issues
item.description:
The reporting slice: a citizen reports, anyone reads, an agency triages.

Run top to bottom — each request feeds the next through collection variables.

request.description: Signs in a seeded account. `npm run seed` creates it; every seeded account shares {{demo_password}}.
Signs in a seeded account. `npm run seed` creates it; every seeded account shares {{demo_password}}.
Only a CITIZEN may report. `reportedBy` is taken from the token and `status` from the schema default, so neither can be supplied here.
The civic record is public: a transparency platform that requires a login is not one.
Filters: `status`, `category`, `reportedBy`. Paging: `limit` (default 20, max 100) and `offset`. An unknown enum value is a 400.

item.name: Read one issue — no token needed

request.description: A malformed id returns 400 via ParseObjectIdPipe; a well-formed but unknown id returns 404.
Ownership, not role, is the gate here — and only while the issue is still OPEN. An admin editing someone else’s issue gets the same 403.
Creates the issue that the next request marks as a duplicate of the first.
DUPLICATE requires a `duplicateOf` naming an existing, different issue.
REJECTED requires a `reason`. Rejection is the recorded alternative to deleting a report — there is no DELETE route.

item.name: Issues — guardrails
item.description: Every rule the reporting slice enforces, asserted as a refusal.

item.name: Sign in as a second citizen

request.description: Signs in a seeded account. `npm run seed` creates it; every seeded account shares {{demo_password}}.
An OPEN issue for the ownership checks below — the issue from the Issues folder has already been rejected by this point.
Every route is default-deny; reporting is not @Public().
Agencies triage; they do not file reports. @Roles(CITIZEN) on the route.
CreateIssueDto declares no `status`, so forbidNonWhitelisted refuses it as an unknown property. The gate is structural, not validated.

item.name: Guardrails
item.description: Every one of these is enforced server-side, not by hiding a control in a UI. Run this folder as a security regression suite — all requests assert their status code.

request.description: This folder is self-contained, so it obtains its own tokens rather than depending on the folders above.
Captures a non-privileged token for the 403 checks below, and a user id for the escalation attempts.

RegisterDto has no `roles` field at all, so this is rejected as an unknown property by the global forbidNonWhitelisted pipe — a 400 because there is nothing to submit, not because a validator turned it down. Agencies are the authoritative owners of issues, so that authority cannot be claimed by anyone who can reach the signup form.
Same gate, same reason: there is no field to put it in.

item.name: Even a harmless roles field is refused

request.description: CITIZEN is what registration assigns anyway — and it is still a 400. That is the point: the field does not exist, so there is no gate to get wrong.
The guards are global, so a route is protected by default. A route added in a later phase that forgets its guard still fails closed.
Malformed, expired and wrongly-signed tokens are all just 'no'.
Authenticated, but a CITIZEN holds no ADMIN role.
The privilege-escalation route is itself ADMIN-only.
Note the message, and compare it with the next request.
